[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent Composite ABB**: [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-REF-1.6.02 — Cloud and Infrastructure Security Composite ABB](GUID-SEC-CLOUD-REF-1.6.02.md)
- **Domain**: Inbound File Scanning — Malware and Virus Detection at Ingest Boundaries
- **Capability Statement**: Establishes the architectural capability to inspect all inbound file streams destined for Platform Gainwell storage volumes and data systems — intercepting malicious content before it reaches any destination, quarantining infected objects, and alerting the Security Operations Center in real time
page_texts.5:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Fail-closed staging/landing zone architecture: all inbound files **SHALL** land in a transient staging store before any promotion to a destination volume
- Antivirus and malware scan execution against all files at the ingest boundary, regardless of file type, size class, or originating system
- Binary scan-result tagging on each scanned object (`CLEAN`, `INFECTED`, `PENDING`, `ERROR`) with engine version and scan timestamp metadata
- Infected object quarantine: automatic redirection of `INFECTED`-tagged objects to an isolated quarantine store; all download or forward operations on quarantined objects **SHALL** be denied by policy
- Scan engine definition currency: antivirus signature and heuristic definitions **SHALL** be refreshed on a minimum daily cadence via an automated pipeline
- Real-time SOC alerting: `INFECTED` outcomes **SHALL** trigger structured alert events to the Security Operations Center within a defined latency SLO
- Audit logging: all scan events — both `CLEAN` and `INFECTED` — **SHALL** be recorded to an immutable log store
- Multi-channel coverage: the pattern applies uniformly to all Platform Gainwell ingest channels in scope (see Out of Scope below for v1 deferral list)

**Out of Scope**:
- Runtime behavioral detection of executing workloads (Workload Protection ABB: [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-WORKLOAD-PROT-2.6.04](GUID-SEC-CLOUD-WORKLOAD-PROT-2.6.04.md))
- Data Loss Prevention scanning for sensitive data exfiltration (Data Security domain: GUID-SEC-DATA-DLP-2.5.05)
- Scanning of data already at rest in existing destination volumes — this ABB governs ingest-time scanning only
- Kafka binary payload scanning and database LOB column import scanning — deferred to a future ABB revision
- Antivirus agent deployment on EC2 instances or container images (Vulnerability Management ABB: [GUID-SEC-CLOUD-VULN-MGMT-2.6.09](GUID-SEC-CLOUD-VULN-MGMT-2.6.09.md))
- Security controls, configuration requirements, and compliance mandates (belong in `standards/security/`)
- Solution Building Blocks and vendor-specific tooling (Phase E–F outputs)

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

**1. Ingest Boundary is the Control Point**
The scan intercept **SHALL** operate at the ingest boundary — files **SHALL NOT** be written to any destination volume until a scan result of `CLEAN` has been confirmed. A system that writes files to a destination before scanning is non-compliant with this ABB regardless of any post-write scan capability.

**2. Fail-Closed by Design**
If the scan engine is unavailable, degraded, or returns an `ERROR` result, the file **SHALL NOT** be promoted to the destination. The system **SHALL** fail closed. Fail-open configurations — where unavailability of the scan engine permits file promotion — are architecturally prohibited.

**3. Intercept Before Destination, Quarantine on Detection**
An `INFECTED` scan result **SHALL** result in immediate quarantine of the object and denial of all forward operations. The infected object **SHALL NOT** be copied to, referenced by, or accessible from any downstream system. Quarantine **SHALL** be enforced at the storage policy layer, not solely at the application layer.

**4. Definition Currency is Non-Negotiable**
Scan engine signature definitions **SHALL** be refreshed at a minimum daily cadence via an automated, monitored pipeline. Signature staleness beyond 24 hours **SHALL** generate an operational alert. Manual-only definition update processes are architecturally prohibited for production ingest channels.

**5. Every Scan Event is an Audit Record**
Both `CLEAN` and `INFECTED` scan outcomes **SHALL** be recorded to an immutable audit log. Log records **SHALL** include: scanned object identifier, source channel, scan result, engine version, definition version, and scan timestamp. Audit logs **SHALL** be protected from modification or deletion.

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#staging--landing-zone-isolation]

#### Staging / Landing Zone Isolation

**Architectural intent**: Ensure no inbound file can reach a destination volume without passing through a controlled scan gate. The landing zone acts as a mandatory security checkpoint — not a convenience buffer.

**Design guidance**:
- A staging store (landing zone) **SHALL** be provisioned as a distinct logical boundary from all destination stores; destination write permissions **SHALL NOT** be granted to the ingesting identity
- Object promotion from landing zone to destination **SHALL** be triggered only by a confirmed `CLEAN` scan result from the scan engine
- IAM or equivalent access policies **SHALL** enforce the one-way promotion gate; no direct path from source to destination **SHALL** exist outside the scan workflow
- The landing zone **SHALL** have an object expiry or lifecycle policy to prevent indefinite accumulation of unscanned objects
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#scan-engine-execution]

#### Scan Engine Execution

**Architectural intent**: Provide a deterministic, auditable scan execution path for every inbound object, regardless of ingest channel.

**Design guidance**:
- The scan engine **SHALL** be invoked synchronously within the ingest workflow before any promotion decision is made
- Each scan invocation **SHALL** produce a structured result containing at minimum: result code (`CLEAN` / `INFECTED` / `ERROR`), threat name (if `INFECTED`), engine version, and definition version
- Scan engine capacity **SHALL** be sized to handle peak ingest throughput with a defined latency SLO; scan latency that materially degrades ingest SLAs **SHALL** trigger an architecture review
- Archive and compressed file formats (ZIP, TAR, GZIP) **SHALL** be recursively inspected; zip bomb and nested archive depth limits **SHALL** be configured
- Files exceeding configurable size thresholds **SHOULD** be handled by a dedicated large-file scan path; size-based bypass is architecturally prohibited
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#quarantine-store]

#### Quarantine Store

**Architectural intent**: Provide an isolated, access-controlled store for infected objects that preserves forensic integrity while preventing any downstream access.

**Design guidance**:
- The quarantine store **SHALL** be a separate logical boundary from both the landing zone and all destination stores
- All access to the quarantine store **SHALL** be denied by default; only Security Operations and forensics roles **SHALL** hold read access, and only via explicit policy grant
- Infected objects in the quarantine store **SHALL NOT** be automatically deleted; a documented retention and destruction policy **SHALL** govern lifecycle, including legal hold provisions
- Quarantine store encryption **SHALL** use a dedicated key with access restricted to Security Operations; the key **SHALL NOT** be shared with any destination store
- The quarantine store **SHALL** inherit at minimum the same data classification as the originating ingest channel
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#scan-result-tagging-and-metadata]

#### Scan Result Tagging and Metadata

**Architectural intent**: Create a durable, queryable audit trail on each scanned object that supports operational monitoring, incident investigation, and compliance reporting.

**Design guidance**:
- Scanned objects **SHALL** be tagged with: `scan-status` (`CLEAN` / `INFECTED` / `PENDING` / `ERROR`), `scan-engine-version`, `scan-definition-version`, `scan-timestamp` (ISO 8601 UTC)
- `INFECTED` objects **SHALL** additionally carry a `scan-threat-name` tag containing the detected signature name
- Tags **SHALL** be immutable post-scan; no application-layer process **SHALL** be granted permission to modify scan result tags
- Object promotion to destination **SHALL** be conditioned on the presence of a `scan-status: CLEAN` tag; absence of the tag **SHALL** be treated as an `ERROR` condition
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#soc-alerting]

#### SOC Alerting

**Architectural intent**: Ensure the Security Operations Center receives structured, actionable, low-latency notification on every `INFECTED` detection.

**Design guidance**:
- Every `INFECTED` scan result **SHALL** generate a structured alert event containing: object identifier, source ingest channel, threat name, uploader identity, timestamp, and quarantine store reference
- Alert events **SHALL** be delivered to the SOC via an enterprise-standard event routing path (e.g., event bus → notification service → SIEM integration); the specific technology is an SBB-level decision
- Alert delivery latency **SHALL** not exceed a defined SLO measured from scan completion; the SLO value **SHALL** be documented in the paired Reference Architecture Document
- Alert events **SHALL** be idempotent and deduplicated; duplicate alerts for the same scan event **SHALL NOT** generate duplicate incident tickets
- SOC alert schema **SHALL** align with the enterprise monitoring and alerting conventions defined in [GUID-SEC-SECOPS-MON-2.1.01](../SecOps/GUID-SEC-SECOPS-MON-2.1.01.md)
page_texts.14:
[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#definition-currency-pipeline]

#### Definition Currency Pipeline

**Architectural intent**: Maintain scan engine effectiveness against current threat signatures without manual operational intervention.

**Design guidance**:
- Signature and heuristic definition refresh **SHALL** be automated via a scheduled pipeline; the minimum cadence is daily
- The update pipeline **SHALL** include: definition source pull → engine rebuild or layer update → deployment to scan execution environment → verification of successful update
- Definition staleness beyond 24 hours **SHALL** generate an operational alert to platform engineering; staleness beyond 48 hours **SHALL** escalate to Security Operations
- Definition update pipeline failures **SHALL NOT** leave the scan engine running with a partially updated definition set; the prior known-good definition version **SHALL** be retained as the active fallback
- The definition update process **SHALL** be monitored and its status observable through the platform's standard operational dashboards

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming / Providing ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ingest Channel Trigger | Inbound | Calling ingest channel (Transfer Family, API Gateway, S3 Event) | File arrival event that initiates the scan workflow |
| Scan Result Event | Outbound | SOC Alerting / SIEM | Structured scan result event emitted on each scan completion |
| Object Promotion Signal | Outbound | Destination store policy / workflow | `CLEAN` confirmation that gates object promotion |
| Quarantine Write | Outbound | Quarantine Store | Secure transfer of `INFECTED` objects to quarantine boundary |
| Definition Update Feed | Inbound | Definition source (vendor feed, open-source update server) | Upstream signature and heuristic definition refresh |
| Audit Log Write | Outbound | [GUID-SEC-SECOPS-MON-2.1.01](../SecOps/GUID-SEC-SECOPS-MON-2.1.01.md) | Immutable scan event audit record |

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

This ABB advances the **Data pillar** of Zero Trust by enforcing explicit verification of every inbound data object before it is granted access to any protected data store. No trust is extended to inbound file streams based on the identity of the sender or the transport protocol alone — every object is independently verified at the data layer.

It also advances the **Networks pillar** by establishing a mandatory traffic inspection point at every ingest boundary, ensuring that the network path from sender to destination always passes through a security verification layer.

Specifically:
- The staging/landing zone architecture implements the Zero Trust principle of denying implicit trust — no file transitions from untrusted ingest to trusted destination without explicit positive verification
- The fail-closed posture implements the Zero Trust principle of assuming breach — the default outcome on uncertainty is denial, not admission

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the following NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control families:

| Control Family | Architectural Intent Addressed |
|---|---|
| **SI — System and Information Integrity** | The scan execution and definition currency capabilities directly address the architectural intent of protecting platform systems from malicious code delivered via inbound file transfers |
| **IR — Incident Response** | The SOC alerting and structured event emission capabilities enable the architectural capacity to detect, report, and initiate response to malicious content events |
| **AU — Audit and Accountability** | The immutable scan event audit logging capability enables the architectural capacity to record and protect evidence of all scan outcomes, supporting investigation and accountability |
| **AC — Access Control** | The quarantine store access restriction and object promotion gate implement the architectural intent of restricting access to objects based on verified integrity status |

> This section documents architectural intent alignment only. Specific control implementation requirements are governed by `standards/security/`.

[strategy/guidance/security/Cloud-and-Infrastructure/GUID-SEC-CLOUD-FILE-SCAN-2.6.11.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- **Ingest channel integration required**: This ABB defines the architectural pattern; realization requires each ingest channel owner (Transfer Family, API Gateway, S3-native, etc.) to integrate with the scan workflow. Channel owners **SHALL** not bypass the landing zone pattern.
- **Cross-domain dependency**: SOC alerting integration depends on the SecOps monitoring and alerting architecture ([GUID-SEC-SECOPS-MON-2.1.01](../SecOps/GUID-SEC-SECOPS-MON-2.1.01.md)) being in place for the alert routing path.
- **Scan engine selection is an SBB decision**: This ABB is vendor- and engine-agnostic. The selection of ClamAV, Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3, or a commercial AV SDK is governed by an Architecture Decision Record and realized in Phase E–F Solution Building Blocks.
- **Data classification inheritance**: The quarantine store and audit log **SHALL** inherit the data classification of the highest-classified ingest channel they serve.
- **PHI scope**: Ingest channels that carry PHI-classified data are subject to additional HIPAA safeguard requirements that **SHALL** be addressed at the SBB level.
